memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses at Mount Sinai, "Speak to the Israelites and say
to them: 'When you enter the land I am going to give you, the land
itself must observe a sabbath to the LORD'" - Lev 25:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gave the Sabbath rest not only to people but to the soil itself.
Every seventh year the fields were to lie fallow. Even the land was
invited to rest before the LORD.

There is something humbling in this. We tend to think the world exists
to be used, squeezed for every ounce of productivity. God says
otherwise. His creation has a rhythm of work and rest built into it by
design.

Notice too where this was spoken: at Mount Sinai. Before Israel had even
entered the land, before there was a single field to leave fallow, God
was already teaching them how to live there. He was shaping their hearts
in advance.

Dear friend, we resist rest because we fear falling behind. But the God
who made the land also sustains it. A field left fallow was not a field
abandoned; it was a field entrusted to God.

Jesus said, come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will
give you rest (Matt 11:28). The Sabbath principle running through
Scripture is not a burden but a mercy. We are creatures, not machines.

Where in your life have you refused to leave anything fallow? Ask God to
teach you His rhythm of trust.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I treat rest as a weakness or as God's design?
2. What part of my life have I never allowed to lie fallow?
3. Do I truly believe God can sustain what I set down?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You built rest into Your very creation. Teach me to trust You
enough to stop, and help me find my deepest rest in Jesus. Amen.
